messages:
alice: heads-up — seeing a tiny but consistent spike in TLS handshake sampling failures (~0.01%) across eu-west and ap-south. Error looks like 'session ticket HMAC mismatch' and sometimes an entropy-related log. anyone touched RBAC/KMS yesterday? :eyes:

cert-rotator-bot: Rotator job 2026-03-20T02:14Z attempted signing with key version v7 -> rotated to v8 at 2026-03-20T02:10Z. No retries flagged.

dan: can you paste a log example? grep + a 1-2 line snippet is enough.

alice: sure — snippet from proxy logs: 
```
2026-03-20T02:14:05Z proxy-eu-west-1 tls: session ticket HMAC mismatch (id=0x7fa2)
2026-03-20T02:14:05Z proxy-eu-west-1 kms: DecryptDenied key=projects/prod/locations/global/keyRings/rotator/cryptoKeys/rotator-key
```

maria: we did a IAM policy prune yesterday at 01:50Z to remove some overprivileged service accounts. Did that affect the rotator SA perms?

ryan: checking KMS audit: I see a burst of 403s from `serviceAccount:rotator@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` at 02:14:04–02:14:10Z. Looks like `kms.cryptoKeys.decrypt` denied for v7 when rotator tried to unwrap old tickets. internal link: https://logs.redwood/abcdef (redacted)

dan: ok — that lines up. hypothesis: rotator rotated signing key to v8, but some proxies still try to validate tickets issued under v7 and need Decrypt permission to unwrap HMAC state. If IAM prune removed `kms:Decrypt` from rotator or a proxy role, that would cause validation mismatch.

alice: makes sense. Do we have a rollout window where proxies switched to the new code path that requires KMS for ticket verification? We increased handshake sampling rate in eu-west last week fwiw.

maria: yes there was a small feature roll (ticket-keystore-2026-03-18) that tightened server-side validation and added an optional call to KMS for ticket integrity checks. The intent was to rely on cached keys but fallback to KMS if cache missed.

ryan: audit logs show the rotator's cache miss rate spiked right after rotation and the KMS denies coincide with that. So two contributing factors: prune removed permissions, and cache miss meant runtime attempted KMS decrypts.

dan: short-term mitigation options:
- re-grant `kms:Decrypt` to rotator SA (fast)
- temporarily revert the strict validation flag on proxies (`ENABLE_STRICT_TICKET_VALIDATION=false`)
- bump ticket cache TTL to reduce KMS hits
Which do we want?

sre-oncall: prefer re-grant + bump TTL. Reverting validation is risky for security. Also create an alert if error rate > 0.1% for 10m.

maria: +1 to grant and TTL bump. I'll submit a least-privilege exception for rotator SA while we re-evaluate IAM prune. Also will add an audit log watch for future prunes.

alice: tia. Can someone run the commands to re-add kms:Decrypt for `rotator` and then post the IAM diff?

ryan: done — re-added `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` to `serviceAccount:rotator@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com`. IAM diff: `+ bindings: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter -> rotator`. Pushed to infra-change PR #4621.

dan: I'll open a quick rollback flag in the rotator pipeline to block further rotations until we confirm stable. Also pushed a TTL change to ticket cache (`CACHE_TICKET_TTL=15m -> 45m`) to prod canary.

cert-rotator-bot: Incident INC-2026-74 created: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-74 — assigned to maria, oncall, and alice. Playbook: https://handbook.redwood/mtls-ticket-playbook

alice: nice. Next steps: 1) monitor sampling for 30m, 2) run e2e in eu-west canary to validate old ticket acceptance, 3) schedule follow-up to tighten IAM prune process so rotator SA not impacted.

sre-oncall: set alert: `sum(errors.session_ticket_hmac_mismatch) / sum(handshakes) > 0.001 for 10m` -> page oncall.

maria: I'll coordinate the IAM follow-up and add a test to the prune job to ensure `kms:Decrypt` isn't removed from any known service principals.

alice: thanks everyone :lock: — keeping eyes on it.

ryan: logs look stable at +20m. errors dropped to baseline. Will post final update in 30m. :white_check_mark:
